page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, provisioned with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 64.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 48 MB of L3 cache, instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. This instance does not include a GPU, but it bundles 644 GB of direct-attached local SSD temporary storage alongside support for remote premium storage.

Benchmark evaluations position the D16ds_v5 consistently within the middle 50% across most standard computational workloads. The system achieves a PassMark CPU score of 21,192.15 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,540.0, with single-core Geekbench measuring 1,570.0. Memory throughput reaches 99.32 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 58.27 GB/sec for large-block writes. In network and transactional services, the instance handles 15.82 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves static web serving throughput of 21.35 GB/sec. When evaluating CPU-based machine learning inference, prompt processing for small 135M models averages 1,107.85 tokens/sec, while small model text generation performs in the upper 25% bracket at 265.09 tokens/sec.

Resource allocation delivers balanced cost efficiency by offering dedicated execution threads and bundled high-speed local disk without requiring external volume attachment for ephemeral scratch space. The main tradeoff involves thread topology: because 16 vCPUs map to 8 physical execution cores, heavy parallel loads requiring pure execution pipeline isolation may see thread contention compared to dedicated single-thread core instances. Without GPU acceleration, parallel tensor workloads are limited to lightweight AVX-512 VNNI execution. The configuration is optimal for production relational databases, Redis caching layers, web application backends, software compilation pipelines, and ETL processing.

The instance incorporates 644 GB of bundled local SSD storage and lacks hardware GPU acceleration. Performance benchmarks demonstrate consistent mid-tier results across compute, memory, and application operations, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,540.0, 15.82 million Redis SET operations per second, and 21.35 GB/sec in static web serving.
